deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is a working draft from the period of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (1854). The previous page is Art. 11 of that text; the next page carries a letter dated Feb. 1853. The page holds three things.

(a) Top lines. A non-mathematical note to a landlord ('Ew. Wohlgeboren'). Riemann gives notice that he will not keep his room next semester.

(b) Draft of the opening summary. The essay has two parts. Part 1 is a history of the investigations and views on arbitrary ('graphically given') functions and their representability by trigonometric series. For it Riemann used hints ('Winke') from the famous mathematician who wrote the first thorough work on the subject, i.e. Dirichlet. Part 2 investigates representability in the cases not yet treated. An alternative draft in the right column adds that this required first fixing the concept of the definite integral and the scope of its validity. This is essentially the wording of the published introduction.

(c) Examples illustrating the general considerations (they became Art. 6 of the published text).

Example 1: a function discontinuous on a dense set but integrable.
- Let (x) = x − nearest integer, with (x) = 0 when x is a half-integer, the mean of ±1/2.
- Define f(x) = Σ_{m≥1} (mx)/m².
- Convergence: |(mx)| ≤ 1/2 and Σ 1/m² converges, so the series converges absolutely and uniformly for all x. This step is implicit on the page and is mine.
- Let x = p/(2n) with gcd(p,n) = 1 (p is then odd). Then mx is a half-integer exactly when m = n(2k+1), k ≥ 0. This step is mine.
- At each such point (mx) jumps from +1/2 (left limit) to −1/2 (right limit), while the value there is 0. All other terms are continuous at x.
- Uniform convergence allows taking limits term by term. Hence f(x+0) − f(x) = Σ_k (−1/2)/(n²(2k+1)²) = −(1/(2n²))(1 + 1/9 + 1/25 + …) = −π²/(16n²).
- Likewise f(x−0) = f(x) + π²/(16n²).
- At all other x every term is continuous, so f(x±0) = f(x).
- Conclusion: f is discontinuous at exactly the rationals with even denominator in lowest terms. The jump π²/(8n²) shrinks as the denominator grows; f is continuous elsewhere and 'admits an integration'.
- Right-column variant: this is an example of a function not continuous in any subinterval of (a,b) that is nevertheless integrable.

Example 2: a non-integrable function, Dirichlet's.
- φ(x) = 1 for commensurable (rational) x and 2 for incommensurable x.
- In every subinterval Δ the oscillation is 1, however small the mesh d.
- So Σ (oscillation × length) stays equal to b − a and does not tend to 0. Hence Riemann's integrability criterion fails.
- Final fragments: '[this] criterion for the validity of integration [to] add'.
errors: No mathematical errors. The jump formula f(x±0) = f(x) ∓ π²/(16n²) at x = p/(2n) is correct and matches the published Art. 6.

Minor gaps, filled in the reconstruction: uniform convergence, which justifies taking one-sided limits term by term, is not stated on the page. Nor is the fact that the jumping terms are exactly m = n·(odd).

results.what: f(x) = Σ (nx)/n²: integrable function discontinuous at every rational with even denominator, with jumps π²/(8n²)
results.modern_name: Riemann's example of a Riemann-integrable function with a dense set of discontinuities

results.what: Function equal to 1 on rationals and 2 on irrationals is not integrable, since Σ oscillation × length = b − a
results.modern_name: Dirichlet function; failure of Riemann's integrability criterion
results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet (1829) for the function; Riemann (1854) for the criterion

results.what: Draft of the two-part introduction to the Habilitationsschrift, acknowledging Dirichlet's hints

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the published introduction and of Art. 6 of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift. The examples and formulas are well known as his. Only small textual variants are of interest: explicit use of Dirichlet's function with the 'b − a' oscillation sum, and the phrase 'graphically given' functions.

checkable.asserts: Bound π²/12 on |f(x)|, giving uniform convergence of Σ (nx)/n²

transcription_corrections: Right column: 'zeigt ein Beispiel einer Function, welche f in keinem Theile…' — the stray 'f' is probably a struck or misread character; the sense is 'welche in keinem Theile des Intervalls a…b stetig ist, aber dennoch einer Integration fähig ist'.
'Zur Erläuterung des ersten Falles, wo die Function unendlich[?] oft[?] [...] wird' most likely reads '…unendlich oft unstetig wird'.
The condition 'wo p und n relative Primzahlen' is part of the struck/inserted parenthesis, consistent with the published Art. 6.
Final lines read roughly 'Dieses Kriterium für die Gültigkeit der Integration … hinzufügen'; the line before ('und …') is struck.
